<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via applyRemoteMetadataMutation (symbol, a method of class ProtocolClassHeadFacet))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via applyRemoteMetadataMutation (symbol, a method of class ProtocolClassHeadFacet))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via applyRemoteMetadataMutation (symbol, a method of class ProtocolClassHeadFacet))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via revertCommit (symbol, a method of class ProtocolPackageCommitsFacet))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `60cea19191440b4b7d3f39b2306ca74b21b5b8a2` — the merge of head `3f3f2b1d68b6496c1b5076a514a46c6e091fc510` into base `6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 60cea19191440b4b7d3f39b2306ca74b21b5b8a2 && git checkout 60cea19191440b4b7d3f39b2306ca74b21b5b8a2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661 3f3f2b1d68b6496c1b5076a514a46c6e091fc510 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661 && git merge --no-ff 3f3f2b1d68b6496c1b5076a514a46c6e091fc510

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Head-sha: `9bcce232f687c76bff7c726b14012a4b7309d6e5`

#32366 is a child of epic #31527, and the epic body says: "The epic seat reviews EVERY child PR, whichever lane builds it, against the three red lines below. A child PR is not ACCEPTed without that record." The seat's own checklist is below; ACCEPT and landing wait for that record at this head.

- **Shape:** draft → `main`. First line `Fixes #32366`, the only closing keyword in the body. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are on their own lines in the body and the changeset; the `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch changeset reads true against the diff.
- **Scope:** 9 files.
  - In the claim's surface: `protocol-registry-hydration.ts`, `protocol-class-head.ts`, `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`, `protocol-package-commits.ts`, `protocol-packageless-overlay-migration.ts`, the new test, the changeset.
  - Outside the claim's surface, both accepted: `protocol.ts`, a 2-line signature forwarder the facade split forces (region `restoreArtifactRegistryView` only; #30020 edits `applySeedBodies` elsewhere in that file); and `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, 3 rows written by the gate's own `--write` for the new pin's double.
- **Seat spot reads:**
  - Tier 2 now reads `readItemFromMetadataService(type, name, packageId ?? undefined)`. Each caller passes the delete's resolved package, `boundPackageOf(existing.package_id)`, the commit's package or the overlay binding. Two callers pass `null` with a reason at the call site: a view name is a global literal, and a cluster peer carries no binding.
  - The silent `catch {}` becomes one `console.warn` naming the item and, for a package-scoped refusal, its holders. That matches the card's "never swallow a package-scoped refusal silently".
- **Dev corrected the seat:** the dispatch named `readCodeLayerForCarryForward` as reading bare. On `origin/main` it already reads `readItemFromMetadataService(type, name, pkg)` (`protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts` L1124, seat re-read), and it is bare only for a package-less save, which D3 answers. It is left unchanged, correctly.
- **Pins and ablation:** 6 cases, alpha and beta each healing their own baseline, plus one-holder and package-less controls. Two ablations: the bare tier-2 read gave 2 red; removing the warn gave 2 red. Both restored, with blob == HEAD.
- **Local:** package suite 22681 passed / 29 skipped; typecheck exit 0; 79 gate families, 76 run, 3 NOT MEASURED (full-build or unshallow prerequisites). Repo-wide `pnpm lint` was left to CI, a declared narrowing. CI at this head is still running.
- **Dev's open question** (peer convergence cannot name the package): not a decision card. The `MetadataMutationEvent` docblock records that the wire carries no binding and must not, and there is no measured pull for a two-holder slotted name across replicas. The seat takes the dev's A: a logged skip, healed on reload. Accepted as is.

epic:#31527#1 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYm8sWjp2Pk76warN7w

**Epic red-line read of #31527 for #32447 (#32366, the registry heal's baseline read), at head `9bcce232`, rendered for the lane's request 6798442734 · 2026-11-11T14:36Z.**

**Verdict: PASS on the red lines. No must-fix. Three should-fix items (one for the lane's contract review on this PR, two carried), and three nits.**

I read the net diff against `origin/main` (9 files, +309 / −11), the PR body, the changeset, card #32366 and its thread, the sibling cards #32365, #32367 and #32407, ADR-0150 on `origin/main`, and the epic body with its rulings and the take-over 6798472014. Nothing was built or run. This is not the contract review: that, ACCEPT and landing stay with `domain:server#4`.

### 1. ADR-0150 D3, D4, D5: agrees

- **D3, never a guess.**
  - Tier 2 now reads `readItemFromMetadataService(type, name, packageId ?? undefined)`. For a type the service stores per `(package, name)`, `readStoreEntry` answers a read naming P with P's slot or a settled miss, never another package's item. A type outside that set is still read by name, so nothing moves for it.
  - Every caller passes the package of the row it removed: the delete door's resolved address (both repository sites), `boundPackageOf(existing.package_id)` on the legacy path, the commit's package in `revertCommit`, and step 4's binding in the migration.
  - The three `null` callers each have a reason that holds: a view name is a bucket-1 literal; a package-less row is D3's caller with no package; the peer has no binding to name (S2).
- **D4, holders.** The baseline goes back into the bare slot carrying its own `_packageId`, so `overlaySlotBinding` binds it to P and Q's exact address is never served it. The registry's holder count for the name is what it was while P's row sat in that slot.
- **D5, never swallowed.**
  - The outer `catch` logs once. A package-scoped refusal is recognised by the one recogniser (`packageScopedRefusalOf`) and printed with the store's own message, which names every holder. No new shape or code is minted.
  - The heal is no door: the delete has committed and its receipt is unchanged, so a log line is the right carrier, and no `409` is owed here.
  - The by-name door asks the service before the registry, so a bare read of the name still answers the `409` after a heal that stopped.
- **A refusal is not read as a miss.** After the refused bare read the walk registers nothing and retires nothing. The pin holds both.
- **`readCodeLayerForCarryForward`: the dev's correction holds.** At this head it reads with the save's package (`storedBodyForCarryForward` passes `args.packageId`) and has no `catch`. The card's second half is closed by measurement, and the PR body says so.
- **Red line 3.** One-holder controls are pinned for a package-less row and for the holder's own row. One case is not: S1.

### 2. Siblings and scope: clean

- **#32365** (a package-less item beside one holder; an environment row beside two; a disabled holder first): untouched. `package-slotted-store.ts` and `registry.ts` are not in the diff. The heal's `null` read inherits whatever that card rules (S3).
- **#32367** (Console nav action): no `ui/**` file.
- **#32407** (the package-less refusal outside `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES`, and the layered door): `protocol-exact-qualifier.ts` and `protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts` are untouched.
- **#32183 / #32327 and #31699 / #32214:** no type set, loader or served-set filter is touched.
- **Surface beyond the claim:** the `protocol.ts` forwarder and three `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` rows. Both follow from the change and are declared.
- **Nothing is half-done** inside the card's wording, except the row S1 names.

### 3. Order: clear

- **`main`** is at `87c0407d`, one commit past this head's merge base, with no file in common. `git merge-tree` is clean.
- **#32214** at `f9f589da`: no file in common, and the trial merge is clean. It adds `email_template` to `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES`, so this tier-2 read names the package for that type too once both land. That is the intended direction. See S1's carry-in.
- **#32327** at `1b655c3c`: no file in common. The trial merge reports one conflict, in `packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts`. It is #32327's own against `main` (the same conflict appears merging it with `main` alone), not this PR's.
- **The new REQUIRED parameter.** Neither #32214 nor #32327 adds a caller of `restoreArtifactRegistryView`, so neither breaks on it. A caller added later answers the question at compile time, which is the point of making it required.

### Owed items

- **S1, should-fix, on this PR, for the lane's contract review: a removed row bound to a package that is not the holder.**
  - The changeset says "A name one package holds heals as it did". By reading, that holds when the row's package is none or the holder itself.
  - For a row bound to another package, tier 2 now asks the service for that package. The store answers a settled miss, and tier 3 retires the entry. `main` read bare and re-registered the one holder's baseline.
  - The case that matters is the App's pair row of a declared override (ADR-0146; `action` is an open type, #30065). The delete door resolves the pair's id, and the service holds nothing for a pair.
  - Reach is narrow: tier 1 heals first whenever the registry holds the base's composite slot. Neither answer is a guess, so this is no red line.
  - Do one of two things. Either read the base for a pair row and pin it, or state in the changeset that such a row now retires. Either way, add the one-holder control with a row bound to a non-holder package.
  - Carry-in for #32214: `email_template` customizations live in pair rows, so the same question reaches that type when both PRs are on `main`.
- **S2, should-fix, carried as a card under #31527 (not this PR): the peer convergence path.** The dev's out-of-scope finding has no carrier, and it needs one.
  - `applyRemoteMetadataMutation` re-reads the active row and its binding with no package, and heals with no package.
  - On a two-holder name the heal is now a logged skip. For this PR that is accepted, as the lane took it: it guesses nothing.
  - For the card: under D4 the package is part of a row's address, as the member is (#22877). Whether the signal carries it is a wire-contract change and needs its own ruling.
- **S3, should-fix, recorded on #32365 (not this PR): the heal's package-less read.**
  - It inherits that card's three cases unchanged, and takes its fix with no edit here.
  - One question rides it. After a refused package-less heal, the removed row's own entry stays in the bare slot. With no composite holder in the registry, `overlaySlotBinding` reads it as the environment's item until a reload. #32365 rules whether that entry is retired.
- **N1, nit: the level.** AGENTS.md puts "persisted state and runtime state disagree" at `error`. This line says exactly that, at `warn`. The sibling line in the same function is `warn` and `check:durability-log-level` is green. The lane's contract review rules it.
- **N2, nit: the named package in the message.** `''`, `sys_metadata` and an omitted argument are read by the store as no package, but the line prints them as `package '…'`. The three-argument `as any` caller in `protocol.view-container-reset-expansions.test.ts` reaches it with `undefined`.
- **N3, nit: the list of five types** in the changeset and the test header. #32214 lands first and makes it six. On the `main` merge, name the set instead of listing it.

### State at this reading

The head's checks stand at 29 passed, 16 skipped and 5 in progress, with none failed. The PR is a draft.

**Epic red-line re-read of #31527 for #32447 (#32366) at head `6f7a227a13` · 2026-11-11T21:12Z. It follows read 6798706687 at `9bcce232` and the lane's REWORK record 6798737183.** Written by the epic seat after its take-over (comment on #31527).

**Verdict: PASS on the red lines. No must-fix. One should-fix for the lane's contract review (the changeset).**

I read the patch commit `6f7a227a13` (`protocol-registry-hydration.ts`, the heal pin) and the net diff against `origin/main`. Nothing was built or run.

### S1 as patched: agrees with D3 / D4 / D5

`readHealBaseline` reads the removed row's own package first; on a settled miss it reads bare.
- **One holder:** the bare read answers that holder, which is D3's bare resolution and `main`'s outcome. The baseline re-enters carrying the holder's `_packageId`, so D4's binding holds. Not a guess.
- **Two holders:** the refusal is caught only when `packageScopedRefusalOf` recognises it. The base is chosen by the pair relation (`isPairRowRemoval`, the delete door's own predicate) over the refusal's `package` candidates. Exactly one base ⇒ its baseline; zero or several ⇒ the refusal is rethrown and logged, nothing picked, nothing retired. Never a guess.
- **No holder:** a clean miss goes on to tier 3 and retires, as before.
- **Degraded:** the own read's `degraded` returns before any bare read; a degraded bare miss stays degraded. The walk stops without retiring.
- A non-refusal throw from the bare read is rethrown. Non-package candidates (host code, plugin) are never bases, so such a name keeps the refusal.
- Pins: the pair row on one holder and on two, the non-holder control on one holder, the no-pair refusal on two, and the no-holder control. Red line 3's one-holder control is now covered.

N1 (`error`) and N2 (`callerPackageId` via `boundPackageOf`) are in the code.

### Owed, for the lane's contract review (not a red line)

- **S4, should-fix: the changeset was not updated in this round.** It still says "one `warn` line" (now `error`), still lists the five types instead of naming `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES` (N3; #32214 adds `email_template`), and says nothing of the pair row's heal (S1's new behaviour). Fix the text before ACCEPT.
- S2 (peer convergence) and S3 (rides #32365) stand as carried in 6798706687.

### Order

Unchanged from 6798706687. This PR and #32214 share no file. #32214 is the epic's next landing; either may land first.
